# s457 — snapshot: skip building a part whose inputs have not changed

With `--since`, slicer still loads each project and builds each part before it can say `unchanged`, because a part's revision is a hash of its built value. A cheap fingerprint of the files a part reads would let slicer answer before the load, which is the time ork's polling spends. This is a row with an open question; it needs the owner's answers before it is specified.

**Findings:** Follow-up the owner chose on 2026-11-11 while specifying the snapshot deps/--since item: --since drops an unchanged part's value but still loads the store and builds it, because a revision is a hash of the value. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-11** — [decision] Owner decisions (2026-11-11): Q1 option (a): a new fingerprint field beside revision, a hash of (path, mtime_ns, size) for each file the part reads, checked before the load; revision keeps its meaning. Q2 option (a): a part that reads git state (health) is always built.

## Why

- `src/slicer/snapshot.py:14-15` and `:73`: the revision is computed from the built value, so it cannot be known before the store is loaded.
- Measured 2026-11-11: `slicer snapshot --json` takes 129 ms on this repository, against 80 ms for `--version`; the difference is the store load and the part builds.

Open owner questions:

- Q1 the fingerprint. (a) a new `fingerprint` beside `revision`, a hash of `(path, mtime_ns, size)` for each file the part reads (`.slicer/index.json`, `.slicer/slices/`, the relay-run ledger, config), checked before the load; `revision` keeps its meaning (recommended). (b) redefine `revision` as the fingerprint, which changes what existing callers compare.
- Q2 the fall-back when a part reads git state (`health` reads `vcs.merge_in_progress`): (a) such a part is always built (recommended). (b) include the git files it reads in the fingerprint.
